relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.evidence: Note since the document is not available during an OnDelete we will filter by KEY prefix starting with `"tosync:".*`. This is a hard coded implementation.

notable_absence.finding: The Capella twin recorded this OnDelete/document-unavailability fact under behavesDifferentlyUnder (subject eventing:on-delete-handler, object eventing:on-update-handler). That predicate's registered definition is specifically about a clause's behavior changing under an edition or deployment variant (Enterprise/Community/Capella) - not about one handler entry point's call signature lacking a parameter the other has. The already-promoted omitsMutationBody predicate was minted for exactly this OnDelete-vs-OnUpdate signature asymmetry (see its registry note, citing this same batch's genericFlatten/genericRename pages), so this record uses omitsMutationBody instead as the more precise match. Content is otherwise byte-identical to the Capella twin apart from front matter.

cross_component_finding: OnDelete's lack of document-body access forces this handler to fall back to KEY-prefix filtering ('tosync:') instead of the doc.type filter used by every OnUpdate handler in this batch - now captured via omitsMutationBody rather than behavesDifferentlyUnder (see notable_absence).
cross_product_finding: Recurrence of the destination-collection/XCDR hand-off note seen elsewhere in this batch (redactSharedData, genericFlatten, genericRename): "The \"destination\" collection can be shared (or replicated via XCDR to a business partner) too the cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP)." Same pattern, not a new finding.
